deep.reconstruction:
The page holds three full decimal periods of the unit fractions 1/971, 1/967 and 1/953. It continues a descending table of primes (997, 991, 983, 977 on the previous page; 947, 941, 937 on the next). The context is Gauss's work on converting common fractions into decimals (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, arts. 312-318).

Layout:
- The prime is written in the left margin. The faint 5 and 10 in the margin are line counters.
- The period is written in groups of 10 digits, seven groups per line.
- The leading zeros of the expansion are dropped at the start. They reappear at the end, where the repetition restarts.
- The dot over the first digit marks where the period begins. The final underlined group followed by '...' is the beginning repeated, showing the cycle has closed.

(a) p = 971. 1/971 = 0.00 1029866117 4047373841 4006179196 ...
- There are 14 lines of 7 groups. The last group is the repeated '1029866117', so 97 groups = 970 written digits remain.
- The written block is the cyclic shift that starts at the third digit. Its last group '4562306900' ends with the two zeros.
- So the period of 1/971 has length 970 = p-1. In modern terms, 10 is a primitive root mod 971.
- Implicit check (mine): since the order is even, 10^485 = -1 (mod 971). Hence each digit and the digit 485 places later sum to 9.
- I verified this against the page. Written positions 484-490 (line 7, group 7, '9309989701' read from its 4th digit) give 9,9,8,9,7,0,1. These are the 9-complements of expansion digits 0,0,1,0,2,9,8. Line 8 begins '3388...', the complement of '...6611' at written positions 7-10. So the table is internally consistent.

(b) p = 967. 1/967 = 0.00 1034126163 3919338159 ...
- There are 4 full lines (280 digits) plus 4 groups (40 digits), giving 320 written digits.
- Then '0010341261...' restarts the cycle with the two leading zeros.
- So the period is 322 = (967-1)/3, i.e. ord_967(10) = 322. Here 10 is not a primitive root but a cubic residue of index 3.

(c) p = 953. 1/953 = 0.00 1049317943 3368310598 ...
- There are 13 full lines (910 digits) plus 4 groups (40 digits), giving 950 written digits.
- Then '0010493179' restarts the cycle.
- So the period is 952 = p-1, and 10 is a primitive root mod 953.

Vertical bars occur inside the blocks:
- p = 971: line 11, after '...6045';
- p = 967: line 4, after '7269906928';
- p = 953: line 13, after '6232948583'.
They probably mark junctions where one stretch of computation was joined to another, or a check point; their exact purpose is uncertain. The red-ink marks near 967 ('6', '96..') look like later annotations.

The computation itself is ordinary long division, or equivalently successive residues 10^k mod p, carried until remainder 1 recurs.
errors: No arithmetic errors detected in the spot checks: leading digits of all three expansions, period lengths, and the half-period complement for 971.
Line 11 of the 971 block contains a heavily struck-out group followed by '741503 6045|3141091658'. This is a correction during computation; the group boundaries there look irregular in the image.
In the 953 block, line 13, the group is written '623294858 3|' with the final 3 separated by a bar. It is one 10-digit group, 6232948583.
